description:
Guess this is now a place to share my fiddling about with files. Welcome to my random file tweaks!

It's fun to break open files, edit values or swap/insert lines of code and see what happens, because sometimes genuinely interesting or cool things can be the result. This is a compilation of what I've discovered, so I thought I would share them.

I'll try to write up some handwritten guides on how to do things as time goes on. Most edits require digging into the .jar files and making changes using external programs such as Recaf and/or mods like Microforge, but there could be some other more simple edits too.

As a note, I have used ChatGPT to help me along the way. Because I am not looking through thousands of lines of code for a single value to alter. I've got others things to get on with lol. It's a great tool for doing faff work, that would otherwise take me hours to achieve. After all, why have a dog and bark yourself? It has better eyesight than me for finding things.

The file alterations have been tested multiple times, both during and after creation. Firstly, GPT ran the code within itself to ensure there were no conflicts or incorrect values and that the alterations I made worked, then I tested everything in-game and ran roughly 6-12 months (depending on what was changed), in case there were unintended effects. This is how I ironed-out any issues. I couldn't see any in the final versions, but I won't stand on a soap box and shout

"How dare you! They are perfect and you're doing it wrong!"

because games are fickle at the best of times.

You'll need some extra bits and pieces, as listed in the guides.

I'll continue to alter the first post instead of constantly adding comments to say

"Oi, I've done this!"

, adding more tweaks as I discover and construct them. Bookmark the page, if you wish to check for updates now and again. I don't want to keep bumping this to the top. It feels needy.

So, without further ado.

RANDOM GUIDES FOR VARIOUS GAME CHANGES:

Click the titles for links to Pastebin guides.

Thicker Campaign Map Circles

Increases the thickness of the circles that surround fleets, stations, derelicts and such on the System and Hyperspace maps.

This scales as you zoom in and out. Zoom in, the circles become thinner and vice versa. Fully customisable thickness, through simple value edits.

Spoiler[close]

Commission-Based UI Colour Schemes

The colour of the player's campaign map circles and UI will dynamically change, depending on what faction they have a Commission with.

For example, if you take a Hegemony Commission, the circles and UI will change to the faction's orange colour scheme. If you resign the Commission, it will automatically revert back to the standard grey (or whatever colour you have changed it to, in the player.faction file). Grab a new Commission, even with a different faction, it changes again!

It uses whatever RGBA values are present in the .faction files, so if you have altered any faction colour schemes (as I have), it will automatically display those colours. No trickery involved, just pointing it in the right direction. Works with all factions, vanilla and modded.

Improved Scan and Survey Missions

Modifies the starting location of missions to the market/system that generated them.

The vanilla game will always calculate the credit rewards earned from the 0,0 centre of the sector outwards. So if you take a mission from a system that is in, say, the bottom-left corner and the mission target is in the top-right corner, the reward does not take into account the fact that you have to travel across the entire map. You will only be paid as if you were starting from the centre.

Logically, that didn't make sense to me, so this edit changes that calculation! Now the faction market from the system who spawns a mission will be the starting location and the reward calculated properly from there instead. You'll be paid appropriately for the entire journey, from A to B.

Also includes some extra information on how to edit the mission completion time limit, credit rewards and faction reputation changes.

More to come...
